citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: Two processes that run alongside the three phases of work. Monitoring follows how thinking, effort and affect are going, and control acts on that, for example by choosing a strategy, spending more time or revising the goal. The article says each can influence the other and each can be implicit or explicit.

examples: A student judges a word as not yet learned and studies it longer.
A student on a well-practiced task whose monitoring runs without awareness.

labels.en: Monitoring and Control in Parallel With the Task (MASRL)

nonExamples: A teacher deciding what a class should do next.
A grade given after the exam.
